source.title: Beyond Neural Collapse: Task-Intrinsic Geometry Governs Neural Representations in Modular Arithmetic
source.authors: Huihui Tan; Kuo Gai; Shi-Hua Zhang

record.file_problem: none; the full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: The paper analytically compares regularized candidate geometries and derives when a low-rank cyclic code is preferred. It does not reproduce the original training measurements.
record.gate_note: The paper reports no new training curves, train/test accuracy measurements, or training-set-size sweep. Its grokking time-course statements cite prior work and are not rows. Rows below cover its own analytical results on regularization-based preference for the cyclic code.
record.test_reason: The paper is a theoretical analysis. Its only quantitative results (Thm 6.2–6.6, Ex. 6.7) compare two hand-specified terminal classifier geometries, a cyclic rank-2 code and a simplex ETF, under a regularized cross-entropy objective. The ETF is a neural-collapse alternative, not a memorizing solution. The threshold is in regularization strength λ, not training-set size, and no trained model is measured. So these results address a related but different construct, not V5's claim that weight decay favours generalization over memorization, with a critical dataset size and ungrokking. Its hierarchical 'classifier-first' account bears on V2 but is argued from a gradient identity and cited work, not measured. Figure 1 shows PCA circles from the authors' own trained MLP (P=97), but reports no accuracy curves, timing or comparisons across runs.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. Add the other two results. First, once the classifier reaches rank 2, backpropagated gradients lock embedding updates into the classifier plane and weight decay removes orthogonal components. Second, the in-plane objective's minimizers are single-frequency characters of Z/PZ (equal-angle circles). The authors frame grokking as hierarchical (classifier first, then embeddings, then generalization), but this is interpretation rather than a measured result.
record.recipe_differences: A theoretical analysis of terminal candidate geometries and regularized objectives, rather than an empirical training recipe or reproduction. It assumes balanced classes and terminal alignment for key comparisons.
record.method_sensitivity: The derived preference depends on regularization strength and class count: λcrit = Θ(1/K). The Schatten result assumes fixed q < 2; the weight-decay proxy corresponds to q = 1.

fits_no_version.finding: Under assumed terminal alignment, a cyclic rank-2 classifier code loses only O(1) in cross-entropy to a simplex ETF (log I0(1/τ̃)) but saves Θ(K) in Schatten/nuclear-norm cost. The cyclic code is therefore preferred above λcrit=Θ(1/K) (≈2.86e-3 at K=97, τ̃=1).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In modular addition, low-rank/weight-decay regularization above a Θ(1/K) strength makes the cyclic rank-2 (Fourier) classifier geometry globally preferred over the neural-collapse simplex ETF (analytical, not measured in training).

record.problems: The regularization results are analytical comparisons of candidate configurations, not measurements from trained models. They rely on assumptions including balanced classes and terminal alignment; the paper notes limitations including prime moduli and the lack of a sharper dynamical account of when training enters the classifier-first regime.

untested.parts: No train/test accuracy curves, delay, or training-set-size sweep; grokking timing is only cited.
The classifier-first/subspace-locking account is derived, not measured. There is no measured gradual circuit formation, memorization removal, or progress measure anticipating the jump.
No non-algorithmic data and no initialization-scale or weight-norm manipulation.
No generalizing-vs-memorization comparison, no dataset-size variation, no critical dataset size, no ungrokking.
No comparison of learned algorithms across runs, architectures or hyperparameters. Fig. 1 shows a single trained network's cyclic PCA geometry.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's 'tests/T2' and 'V5 supports' are not justified. ETF vs cyclic is a contest between two classifier geometries, not between a generalizing circuit and memorization. All results are closed-form evaluations of assumed configurations. Fig. 1 (PCA circles at P=97 from the authors' MLP) is the only empirical content and reports no training metrics. It could at most loosely illustrate the Fourier/cyclic representation (V2/V6) for a single run, so it is not recorded as a row.

versions.untested_parts: No training/test accuracy time course, chance-level test period, or training-set-size comparison.

No measured gradual circuit formation, removal of memorizing components, or continuous progress measures anticipating a generalization jump. The paper derives a conditional gradient-subspace result, but does not measure the temporal mechanism specified by this version.
No non-algorithmic data or initialization-scale/weight-norm sweep.
No LLM pretraining or fine-tuning on realistic data.

The analysis compares cyclic and simplex candidate geometries under regularization; it does not compare a generalizing circuit with memorization during training, vary dataset size, or test a critical dataset size or ungrokking below it. The threshold derived is in regularization strength, not dataset size.
No comparison of algorithms learned across runs, architectures, or hyperparameters.
No optimizer or numerical-precision controls or artifact tests.

rows.subject: Analytical candidate-geometry comparison: Wcyc versus WETF
rows.size_stated: K classes; asymptotic result as K → ∞
rows.operation_detail: Compared cross-entropy for unit-column cyclic rank-2 and simplex ETF configurations.
rows.value: ΔCE = log I0(1/τ̃) + o(1), an O(1) disadvantage for the cyclic code
rows.note: This quantifies the classification-cost side of the paper's regularization trade-off; it is not a training-curve result.
rows.check: Analytical CE gap between two assumed geometries (cyclic vs ETF) under assumed terminal alignment. It is not a generalizing-vs-memorizing comparison and not a measurement from a trained model, so it does not measure what V5 names.

rows.subject: Analytical candidate-geometry comparison: Wcyc versus WETF
rows.operation_detail: Compared Schatten-q regularization costs of the two candidate configurations.
rows.measure: Difference in q-th powers of Schatten-q norms, Δq = ||Wcyc||Sq^q − ||WETF||Sq^q
rows.note: The paper derives a linear regularization-cost advantage for the cyclic candidate.
rows.check: Schatten-norm cost of two candidate geometries. This is a property of hand-built matrices, not an observed preference in training. It is a different construct from V5's circuit-efficiency-vs-memorization claim.

rows.subject: Analytical candidate-geometry comparison: Wcyc versus WETF
rows.operation_detail: Compared nuclear-norm costs induced by factorized Frobenius weight decay.
rows.value: ||Wcyc||* = √(2K); cyclic code has a Θ(K) regularization advantage
rows.note: The paper identifies the factorized weight-decay proxy with nuclear-norm regularization.
rows.check: Nuclear-norm identity for two constructed matrices. The comparator is a neural-collapse ETF, not memorization.

rows.subject: Analytical candidate-geometry comparison: Wcyc versus WETF
rows.operation_detail: Derived the regularization-strength threshold at which the cyclic candidate has lower total objective than the ETF candidate.

conditions.value: fixed Schatten-q with q < 2, or nuclear norm

rows.value: λcrit ≍ ΔCE/|Δq| = Θ(1/K); above the threshold the cyclic rank-2 configuration has lower regularized objective
rows.note: This is a threshold in regularization strength, not in training-set size.
rows.check: The threshold is in regularization strength (Θ(1/K)) between two generalizing-type geometries. V5's prediction is a critical dataset size and ungrokking, which this cannot show.

rows.subject: Analytical candidate-geometry comparison: Wcyc versus WETF
rows.stage_stated: numerical illustration of the regularized objective comparison
rows.operation_detail: Evaluated the q = 1 trade-off at effective temperature τ̃ = 1.
rows.measure: Cross-entropy gap, nuclear-norm gap, and critical λ
rows.note: This is a numerical evaluation of the paper's analytical comparison, not a reported neural-network training run.
rows.check: A numerical evaluation of the analytical formulas at K=97, not a training run. The values are correct as transcribed.

reader_labels.condition: Analytical comparison of cyclic rank-2 and simplex ETF candidate geometries under fixed q < 2 or nuclear-norm regularization
reader_labels.reason: The cyclic code has a Θ(K) regularization-cost advantage, and the derived objective threshold is Θ(1/K); rows r2–r5 support the regularization-preference component of V5, but do not test its dataset-size or memorization claims.
